title.narrative: Second Disaster Risk Management DPL with Catastrophe Deferred Draw Down Option

description.narrative: The objective of Second Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan with Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option Project for Colombia is to strengthen the Government's program for reducing risks resulting from adverse natural events. The main policy areas are: 1) Strengthening disaster risk management institutional and planning capacity; 2) Strengthening the institutional framework and capacity for including risk assessment in land use planning; and 3) Strengthening policies and tools to reduce risk in the housing sector. The Bank's engagement will focus on: the modernization of the national disaster risk management system; improvements in the application of disaster risk analysis and management in policy making at the sectoral and territorial levels; and strengthening disaster risk management at subnational levels.
To strengthen the Government's program for reducing risks resulting from adverse natural events.

title.narrative: Departments with reports of CCA initiatives or projects under implementation integrating risk understanding and risk reduction actions, implemented within the Territorial CC Mgmt Plan (PIGCCT)

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved (100%). A total of 10 departments (Cundinamarca, Sucre, Córdoba, Nariño, Putumayo, Antioquia, La Guajira,Magdalena, San Andrés and Chocó) have approved projects for climate change adaptation, including actions regarding understanding and reducing risk. Implementation started in six of these 10 projects, all of these within the framework of the PIGCCT.</p>
<p>This indicator was introduced during the second renewal period (2018-2021), replacing RI 5 "Number of municipalities that have agreed to revise their land use plans (POT) with the CAR, under the guidelines of Art. 189, Decree 019 of 2012"  and RI 6 “Number of watershed management plans (POMCAs) that have included DRM in their design” The key expected result for 2015 of RI 5 and 6 was not achieved only 15 POT were revised of a target of 25 POT and only 5 POMCAs included DRM of a target of 25 POMCAS.  However, in 2018 both RIs were achieved (129 municipalities of a target of 25 municipalities revised their POT with CAR; and  58 POMCAs of a target of 60 POMCAs included DRM in their design). </p>

title.narrative: Municipalities that report information on at least one settlement in the inventory of settlements located in high-risk areas, under the guidelines of the MVCT.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved. </strong>A total of 18 new municipalities (of a target of 15 new municipalities) reported at least one settlement in the inventory application. The TA provided was crucial for this achievement.  This indicator was continued through the program’s renewal periods. The key expected result for 2015 (25 municipal inventories) achieved 16% progress, with a total of 4 municipalities that reported inventories of settlements located in high-risk areas. In 2018 only 10 municipalities of a target of 25 municipalities, reported inventories of settlements located in high-risk areas.</p>

title.narrative: Environmental Methodology for Damage, Losses and Needs Assessment (EDANA) designed and implemented.

baseline.value: Environmental Methodology for Damage, Losses and Needs Assessment not designed.

target.value: Environmental Methodology for Damage, Losses and Needs Assessment designed by the MADS and implemented by 5 Regional Environmental Authorities (CARs).

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved (100%). <strong><u>Milestone 1</u></strong>. Preliminary document with the scope and content of the environmental methodology for damage, losses and needs assessment for mainland ecosystems. Progress: achieved in 2019. <strong><u>Milestone 2.</u></strong> Design and validation of the EDANA through four workshops. Progress: achieved. MADS implemented eleven workshops with CARS in  "Corporaciones Autónomas Regionales de Cundinamarca (CAR), de las Cuencas de los Ríos Negro y Nare (CORNARE), de los Valles del Sinú y del San Jorge (CVS), de Chivor (CORPOCHIVOR), de Boyacá (CORPOBOYACA), del Archipiélago de San Andrés, Providencia y Santa Catalina (CORALINA), del Cesar (CORPOCESAR), del Area metropolitana del Valle de Aburra ( AMVA), del Centro de Antioquia (CORANTIOQUIA) y del Atlántico (CRA). <u><strong>Milestone 3.</strong></u> Implementation of the methodology by five pilot Regional Environmental Authorities (CARs). Progress; achieved. The methodology was implemented by CAR, CORNARE, CVS,CORPPOCESAR, CORALINA, AMVA, CORANTIOQUIA, and CORPOBOYACA. </p>

title.narrative: National Technical Assistance (TA) Program in DRM and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), designed, approved and implemented

baseline.value: National TA Program in DRM and CC not designed.

target.value: National TA Program in DRM and CCA, designed, approved and implemented in 5 departments and 2 sectors.

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Overall progress is at 45%.</strong> <u>Milestone<u> </u>1</u>. Proposed preliminary structure of the National TA Program (PNAT) (definition of objective and scope). Progress: achieved. <u>Milestone 2</u>. Design of the PNAT. Progress: achieved. A total of five workshops with the National Planning Department (DNP) and key sectors were organized, where the program’s structure and responsibilities were defined. <u>Milestone 3</u>. PNAT approved. Progress: achieved. <u>Milestone 4</u>. Dissemination of the PNAT. Progress: No progress reported. <u>Milestone 5</u>. Implementation of the PNAT. No progress reported. Governments priorities changed due to COVID-19 pandemic and the 2020 hurricane season.</p>
<p>This indicator was introduced during the second renewal period(2018-2021), replacing the previous indicator “Number of formulated Municipal Plans for Disaster Risk Management under the technical assistance of the National DRM Unit (UNGRD).” The key expected result for 2015 (688 municipalities) was completed above the target, with a total of 813 municipalities (118%). The key expected result for 2018 (886 municipalities) was also completed above the target, with a total of 1,054 municipalities (119%).</p>

title.narrative: DRM instruments for inter-institutional coordination of the National DRM system, designed and approved

baseline.value: Programmatic Component of the National DRM Plan out of date; National Emergency Response Strategy with response protocols outdated;Strategy of Resilient Recovery to Disaster and Climate Change (CC)not designed.

target.value: Three risk management instruments for inter-institutional coordination of the National Disaster Risk Management System (SNGRD), designed and approved: 1. Programmatic component of the National DRM Plan (PNGRD) updated. 2. Five response protocols in the framework of the National Emergency Response Strategy updated. 3. Strategy of Resilient Recovery to Disaster and CC designed.

comment.narrative:
<p>Progress to December 2021:<strong> 83%.</strong></p>

<p>???????<u><strong>(i) Instrument 1.</strong></u> <strong>Programmatic Component of the National DRM Plan (PNGRD)</strong> Updated: Milestone 1. Document with the initial proposal to update the PNGRDprogrammatic component (Progress: 100%). Work has been carried out with 24 sectors, through 120 involved entities and strategic partners, for which the roadmap to meet the established targets was defined. The results from the technical working groups were compiled. Milestone 2. Sectoral dialogue around the programmatic component of the PNGRD, involving 24 sectors was completed. Milestone 3. Adoption of the programmatic component of the PNGRD completed. </p>

<p><strong><u>(ii) Instrument 2.</u> Updated response protocols under the National Emergency Response Strategy:</strong> Milestone 1. Design of 5 response protocols (i. temporarily accommodation protocol; ii. humanitarian aid protocol; iii. search and rescue protocol; iv. water and sanitation protocol; and v. critical incident handling protocol). Progress: achieved, 33.4% of target 33.4%. Milestone 2. Dialogue around response protocols. Progress: 33.3% of target 33.3%. Milestone 3. Adoption of response protocols. Achieved: 33.3% of target 33.3%.</p>

<p><u><strong>(iii) Instrument 3.</strong></u><strong> Strategy of Resilient Recovery to Disaster and Climate Change (CC):</strong> Milestone 1: Designing ofthe Strategy, coordination instruments, roles and responsibilities. Progress: achieved (50%, of the expected 50% target for 2021). Milestone 2. Dialogue around the Strategy of Resilient Recovery. Progress: 0%. No further progress reported, as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2020 hurricane season, which shifted UNGRD’s priorities and disrupted normal work modalities and schedules.  </p>

<p>This indicator was updated during the second renewal period (2018-2021), replacing the previous indicator “The new Agency for the Coordination of the National DRM framework has put in place new instruments for inter-agency Coordination.” The key expected results for 2015 and for  2018 were successfully achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Analysis documents of resettlement processes (relocation) of families in areas of non-mitigable high risk, as an input to the preparation of guidelines for the resettlement of population in such areas

comment.narrative:
<p>Progress to date: Target associated to this results indicator has been achieved (100%). Milestone 1. Undertaking of four institutional working groups. 20% progress reported of 20% target for 2019. Milestone 2. Preparation of two analysis documents of the pilotcases. No further progress was reported (20%) in relation to the 20% defined for 2020. Milestone 3. Inputs for the development of guidelines for resettlement of households in high-risk areas. The final draft of the analysis of two resetlement processes (Salgar and Gramalote) containing the guidelines was completed in October 2020. 30% progress of 30% set for 2021.</p>

<p> </p>

<p>This indicator was introduced during the second renewal period (2018-2021), replacing the previous indicator “Technical assistance and training provided to municipalities for the formulation of the inventory of settlements in high risk areas.” The key expected result for 2015 “250 municipalities” achieved 43.6% progress, with a total of 109 municipalities. The key expected result for 2018 “250 municipalities” was completed above the target, with a total of 265 municipalities (106%).</p>
